featured_reviews.name: Vivek Venugopalan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Amazing place. Way better than the Matunga south indian restaurants.

Shree Muthappan Eating House is a hidden gem at Bhandup on the Jangal Mangal Road. Appam is the speciality of this place and it is totally worth it. The appam is not the sweet round appam but the Malayalam style Appam like dosa. We also had Sada Dosa which was crispy till the last bite. Sambhar and Chutney are one of the best around Mumbai. Your meal should mandatorily end with filter coffee which has the correct amount of decoction and the required sweetness.

Other specialities are Pazham Pori(Kela Bhajji), Parotta, etc. which we couldn't try.

The hotel is clean and the staff are friendly. Owner is a good person and good to have a conversation with.

You can park your two wheelers outside the restaurant on the road.

The rates are way too economical for the quality of food served.

I would surely visit Muthappan Eating house again.

Cheers.

featured_reviews.name: Venkatesh Tadinada
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Santosham recently and absolutely loved the experience. It’s a restaurant serving full South Indian vegetarian meals, with a special focus on Kerala-style cuisine.

The service truly stood out — warm, polite, and always with a genuine smile. They really live up to their name, Santosham (happiness). The entire experience felt welcoming and joyful.

The food was excellent. I especially enjoyed the moong pakora, sambar, avial, poriyal, and the variety of rice dishes — five or six different types, including classic white rice. Every dish was flavorful and well-prepared.

I would happily come back again and would highly recommend this place to anyone who enjoys a good South Indian vegetarian meal.

Your kind words about our team and the spirit of Santosham—happiness—are particularly rewarding. Creating a warm, welcoming, and joyful dining experience is exactly what we strive for every day.

But the highlight? The Veg Schezwan Noodles—packed with bold flavors, just the right spice level, and loaded with fresh veggies. It had that perfect street-style touch while still feeling clean and well-balanced.

The restaurant has a simple yet pleasant ambiance, and the service was prompt and polite. It’s the kind of place where the food speaks louder than the decor—and that’s a good thing!

If you’re in or around Bhandup and love flavorful veg food, Udupi 2 Mumbai is a must-visit. Already planning my next order!

Visited Udupi 2 Mumbai on LBS Road, Bhandup, and it turned out to be an amazing vegetarian restaurant experience. They have ground-floor seating (non-AC) and a first floor with air-conditioned seating. The overall vibe is good, but the first floor is definitely the standout — really comfortable and pleasant.

It’s a pure vegetarian place with a strong South Indian menu: idli, dosa, medu wada, appam and many other varieties — all delicious. They also serve full North Indian meals.

I visited for lunch and we started with paneer spring rolls — had them after ages and it took me straight back to childhood. They were excellent. Then we tried paneer angara with tandoori roti, paneer pahadi kebab, and paneer tikka biryani — yes, complete paneer overload, but everything tasted great. Paneer angara was the highlight for me.
Only disappointment — they don’t serve roomali roti.

The sweet lime soda was a letdown (no fizz, no ice), but apart from that the food was fantastic.
Service was amazing throughout — the staff was attentive, friendly, and very helpful. They even have special seating arrangements for small kids.

Overall, loved the vibe and would definitely visit again.

However, the service was absolutely PATHETIC, DISRESPECTFUL, and MANNERLESS.
Only one staff member behaved politely and served us well. The rest were extremely rude and unprofessional.
One waiter snatched the menu while my mobile was kept on it, moving my phone aside without permission.

featured_reviews.name: Pavan Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
First review
The real stars? That filter coffee—strong, frothy, like a warm hug in a tumbler, cutting through the salty richness perfectly. The payasam, sweet and milky with a cardamom whisper, was pure bliss. Routine dosa didn't disappoint.

Subsequent Review:
When mango season hits Mumbai, Banana Leaf at R City Mall knows exactly how to celebrate it. Their limited-time Mango Mania menu brings together classic South Indian flavors with the king of fruits in a way that feels both comforting and exciting.We started with the ever-reliable Aam Ras with Poori — the kind of pairing that never fails to satisfy. The aam ras was thick, naturally sweet, and bursting with the flavor of ripe mangoes. Paired with soft, fluffy pooris that puffed up perfectly, it made for a simple yet delightful beginning. The Mango Lassi that accompanied it was creamy, chilled, and had just the right balance of sweetness and tang — a refreshing glass that cooled things down instantly.But the real star of the meal was the Mango Pullissery with Neer Dosa. This traditional Kerala-style curry, made with ripe mangoes simmered in a spiced coconut-yogurt gravy (with subtle notes of tamarind and jaggery), delivered a beautiful harmony of sweet, sour, and mildly spicy flavors. The mango pieces were juicy and tender, while the gravy had that signature creamy texture and depth you expect from authentic Kerala sadhya dishes. The neer dosa — thin, lacy, and soft like a delicate crepe — proved to be the perfect companion. It soaked up the pullissery beautifully without overpowering it, letting every bite shine. The combination was so satisfying and well-balanced that by the end of it, our usual post-meal filter coffee felt completely unnecessary. The flavors lingered pleasantly, leaving us content and surprisingly full without any heaviness.The Mango Mania offerings at Banana Leaf strike a nice balance between familiar favorites (like aam ras) and more adventurous regional specials (like the pullissery). The portions were generous, the ingredients tasted fresh, and the execution stayed true to South Indian roots while highlighting the season’s best produce.If you’re a mango lover and enjoy authentic Kerala and South Indian vegetarian fare, this special menu is worth a visit while it lasts. Just come prepared — one taste of that Mango Pullissery with neer dosa, and you might skip the coffee too.
Rating: 4.5/5
Must-try: Mango Pullissery with Neer Dosa

Being from south region native I always preferred to have authentic taste in south Indian dishes. It makes me feel tastefully grounded as well as meets my food flavors expectations. .
DAHl IDLI
Big chunks of Idlis were very soft & tastes yummy in mixture of sweet dahi [curd/lassil. It tastes like brother of Dahi wada if you ever had. There was perfect balance of sweetness, spiciness, sourness & sponginess too.

DILKHUSH DOSA
Will must recommend you try out this dosa which I'm damn sure as per its name It would make your
DIL KHUSH. I already had this named dosa before but here the taste hits next level which makes you remember it.
PIZZA UTHAPPAM
It's fusion of base uthappam & pizza spreads on it. You get dosa & pizza taste together in balanced flavors. Good to try once.
PINEAPPLE SHEERA
Never miss this Indian delicacy at any cost or else you would regret that you hadn't taste. Sheera was very succulent & satisfying in taste. This ending would make you feel coming worthy here.
.
You can easily see their kitchen from seating area Or outside standing area which is neat & clean.
They maintain complete hygiene while preparation of food which I really appreciate as I myself went to kitchen to take some making clips. Visited this place for lunch and had a great experience. The restaurant is clean and hygienic, and it follows a self-service system. Despite being lunch time, it wasn’t very crowded, which made the experience even better. What we tried:
• Gini Dosa (4/5): Loaded with vegetables, mayo, spices, and cheese. Flavorful and filling.
• Rava Masala Dosa (3.5/5): A good rava dosa overall, though it could have been slightly better in taste.
• Onion Uttapam (5/5): Perfect balance of crispy and soft. The sweetness from the caramelized onions really stood out.
• Paniyaram (4/5): Tasty and well-made, but a little on the oily side.
• Dahi Vada (5/5): Absolutely fantastic! Had such a good dahi vada after a long time—definitely a must-try.
• Sambar & Chutneys (5/5): Among the best I’ve had—flavorful and well-balanced.
• Filter Coffee (4/5): Pretty good and satisfying.
Overall, a solid spot for South Indian food with good flavors, fair pricing, and a pleasant dining experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place expecting decent food, but the experience left a lot to be desired. The dahi wada, in particular, was quite disappointing. Instead of having a balanced flavor, it leaned heavily toward sweetness, making it feel more like a dessert than a savory dish. On top of that, the wada itself was unusually small and did not seem properly prepared, both in texture and taste.

What stands out most is that the food feels underwhelming for the amount being charged. A restaurant can charge premium prices, but there should be some effort reflected in taste, portion, and preparation. Sadly, that balance felt missing here.

The ambience works if you just want to sit over tea and spend time, but for food that actually satisfies, there are far better options around.

featured_reviews.name: Abbasali Sorangwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
After trying idli sambar, dahi wada, veg pulao, veg cheese sandwich, and Chinese fried rice over multiple visits, I feel this place is better suited for chai and conversations rather than actual dining.

What disappointed me most was the consistency in poor food quality. I gave the idli sambar two chances on two consecutive weeks, hoping the first experience was just a bad day, but unfortunately, it was the same both times. At ₹70, the idli itself felt poorly prepared, and the sambar had a strange sharp taste, almost acidic, as if too much soda had been added. Instead of feeling satisfying, it actually left me with indigestion after both visits.

Pricing would still be acceptable if the quality matched, but that simply was not the case here. Expensive food is understandable, disappointing food at premium prices is not.

Good spot for chai and hanging out, but if you care about food quality and value, I would avoid coming here for dinner.

featured_reviews.name: Sankalp P
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely Delightful Experience at NEO WELCOME!

We had an amazing time dining at NEO WELCOME. We tried the Mysore Masala Cheese Dosa, and it was simply wow — crispy, flavorful, and cheesy in the best way possible. The Schezwan Fried Rice was tasty and generous in portion, perfect for sharing.

We also tried their Cold Coffee, which was slightly on the sweeter side but still refreshing and enjoyable. The Paneer Paratha and Sada Butter Cheese Dosa were equally satisfying and lived up to the expectations.

What really stood out, apart from the great food, was the excellent service. The staff were very attentive — one of the waiters was constantly going around refilling cold water glasses the moment they were empty. Such thoughtful service is rare and truly appreciated.

Located just outside the station, it’s super convenient to get to. Overall, a fantastic veg restaurant with great food, top-notch service, and a welcoming vibe. Highly recommended and a must-visit!
